en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 18.1.
Hetuduka, Sahetukaduka (The Dyads on Roots, The Dyads on Being Accompanied by Roots)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.

Dependent on a state that is a root-cause and accompanied by a root-cause, a state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause, a state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is both a root-cause and accompanied by a root-cause, and a state that is neither a root-cause and not accompanied by a root-cause, a state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are three; in the object condition, one; in the predominance condition, three ... [and so on] ... in the mutuality condition, five ... [and so on] ... in the result condition, three ... [and so on] ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.

Dependent on a state that is not-root but with-root, there arises a state that is neither-root nor with-root by way of the not-root condition ... (Abbreviated. In the case of the not-root condition, there is one;

in the not-object condition, three; in the not-predominance condition, five; in the not-prenascence condition, four ... [and so on] ... in the not-dissociation condition, one ... [and so on] ... in the not-absence condition, three.
(The sections on "Co-nascent" and "Associated" are also similar to the section on "Dependent.
Root and Object:
A root-conditioned state is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor root-conditioned.
A state that is a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by roots.
A state that is a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not a non-root and not non-accompanied-by-roots.

A state that is a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is both neither a root nor non-accompanied-by-roots and not a non-root and not non-accompanied-by-roots.
Conditioned by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya):
A state that is not-root but with-root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor with-root.
A state that is not-root but with-root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor with-root.

A non-root phenomenon that possesses a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a phenomenon that is neither root nor possesses a root, and for a phenomenon that is neither non-root nor does not possess a root. (Abbreviated.
Both root phenomena possessing roots and non-root phenomena possessing roots are conditions, by way of object-condition, for a phenomenon that is neither root nor possesses a root.

Condition. States that are both root-cause and accompanied by a root-cause, and states that are neither root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause, are conditions, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause. (Abbreviated. One in the case of root-cause;
six in the case of object; two in the case of predominance; four in the case of proximity; five in the case of co-nascence; mutual...
Four [conditions] in dependence; five in decisive support; six in strong-dependence; three in post-nascence; one in repetition; in kamma …pe… three in nutriment;
five in faculty; three in jhāna; five in path; one in association;
three in dissociation …pe… five in non-disappearance. (The Chapter of Questions should be expanded in detail.)
Dependent on a state that is a root-cause and without root-cause, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor without root-cause by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor without root-cause, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor without root-cause by way of root-condition... three. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are four;
under object-condition there are four ... pe ... under prenascence and repetition there is one ... pe ... under result-condition there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are four.
